title: profiling-automation-playground-scripts-catalog
body:
Purpose
This doc is a lightweight catalog and runnable playground for the collection of profiling automation scripts we use to triage serving-runtime performance. It collects small wrappers, CI job snippets, and post-processing helpers that have proven useful for reproducible perf investigations. The emphasis is on: reproducible artifacts (svg/flamegraphs, perf.data, trace.json), CI-friendly wrappers, and low-friction local repro steps.

Scope and intent
- Not a full runbook (see runtime-trace-scripts-and-debug-runbook for that).
- Focused on tooling and scripts that are easy to reuse across experiments (local dev, CI, nightly).
- Includes examples for CPU sampling (perf/freq), eBPF lightweight probes, and GPU wait tracing (NVTX, nsys hooks).
- Target audience: engineers doing iterative perf debugging and build owners who want to add perf checks to CI.

Top-level layout (what this catalog contains)
- scripts/collect-local.sh  -> small bash wrapper to collect perf, nvprof/nsys, and system counters
- scripts/ci-runner.yaml   -> example GitHub Actions job for running a short profiling pass and uploading artifacts to S3
- scripts/stackcollapse-and-flamegraph.sh -> post-process perf script + basic thresholds
- scripts/ebpf-lite-attach.py -> python helper to attach BPF probes for kernel/uv loop stalls
- examples/sample-output/ -> example svg/png and sample perf.data filenames and naming conventions

Why keep a small catalog:
- Single place to iterate on capture short-hands (rarely want entire tracing infra for quick bisects).
- Reduce noise in PRs: add small wrapper PRs instead of ad-hoc commands in issue threads.

Quick local repro (3-minute path)
1) Checkout commit you want to profile.
2) Start the minimal runner (use the same config as CI):
   ./scripts/collect-local.sh --binary ./bin/serve --workload tests/samples/bulk_prompt.json --iters 200 --outdir /tmp/prof-$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
3) Wait for script to finish; artifacts written to outdir.
4) Open flamegraph: outdir/flamegraph-<timestamp>.svg or run ./scripts/stackcollapse-and-flamegraph.sh outdir/perf.data

collect-local.sh (conceptual contents)
- sets up cpu governor to performance for reproducibility
- wraps perf record -F 99 -g -- sleep-style workload sampling for CPU stacks
- optionally runs nsys (NVIDIA Systems Profiler) when GPU workload detected (ENV: PROFILE_GPU=1)
- collects nvidia-smi snapshots, dmesg tail, and /proc/interrupts at start/end
- zips artifacts and writes a small meta.json (commit, kernel, docker image tag)

Example perf record command used by the wrapper
perf record -F 99 -g -a -- sleep 60 
# or attach to pid: perf record -F 99 -g -p $PID -- sleep 30

Post-processing (stackcollapse and flamegraph)
- We rely on Brendan Gregg's stackcollapse-perf.pl and flamegraph.pl (bundled in tools/third_party). The helper script does:
  perf script -i perf.data | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
  ./flamegraph.pl out.folded > flamegraph.svg
- Basic heuristics included: collapse stacks below X% total samples, generate both inclusive/exclusive views (flamegraph and icicle).

CI snippet (github actions) - conceptual
- job: perf-quick-sample
  runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - name: build debug image
      run: make -j && docker build -t runtime-debug:ci -f docker/Dockerfile.debug .
    - name: run profiler
      run: docker run --rm --privileged -v /dev:/dev -e PROFILE_SHORT=1 runtime-debug:ci ./scripts/collect-local.sh --iters 50 --outdir /artifacts
    - name: upload artifacts
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with: name: perf-artifacts-${{ github.sha }}; path: /artifacts
- Keep runs short (30–60s) to reduce cost; validate artifact presence and sample count > threshold as gate.

Nightly/regression pipeline recommendations
- Nightly full sampling (5–10m) for representative workloads (slo p95 tokens latency, throughput tests).
- Store perf.data and collapsed stacks in centralized object store with path schema: prof/<branch-or-commit>/<date>/<target>-perf.data and flamegraph.svg
- Tag runs with git sha, model id, config hash, and machine type (cpu/gpu).

Interpreting results: common signal patterns and quick checks
- Heavy bottom of flamegraph with long C library names (memcpy, memset) -> likely copying/serializing hot path. Check marshalling, flatbuffers, postprocess hooks.
- Kernel/system hotspots (sys_enter_write, schedule) -> IO/blocking/opcache misses; check thread parking, mutex contention.
- Large left-heavy stacks with small width -> few hot functions dominating CPU; that’s often the kernel of perf regressions.
- Wide short stacks -> many callsites with small time (may indicate frequent small allocations).
- GPU wait patterns: long NVTX regions with little GPU sample density -> CPU is waiting on GPU; inspect batch sizes, model shard placement, and nvtx annotations around token generation.
- eBPF signals: syscalls per second spike correlating with context switches -> timer granularity or polling loop issues.

Common traps we hit
- Unreproducible perf.data: caused by governor/power save; always set governor to performance in the wrapper.
- docker/perf mismatch: host kernel needs perf_event_paranoid < 2 and container run with --privileged. Document these in the wrapper.
- Over-zealous sampling: -F too high on small workloads produces empty stacks; use 50-100Hz for short CI samples, 400+ for deep local profiling.

Adding a new script to the catalog (how-to)
1) Add under scripts/ with a short README header describing expected inputs and outputs.
2) Add to scripts/ci-runner.yaml as an optional step; keep default off to avoid runtime costs.
3) Add a test job in .github/workflows/perf-smoke.yml that verifies the script runs and produces an artifact.
4) Link PR to PROF-128 (perf infra epic) and request review from the eng-serving-runtime oncall.

Artifact naming and retention
- Use artifact names: prof-<short-sha>-<target>-<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>.zip
- Inside zip: perf.data, flamegraph.svg, meta.txt, nsys-report.qdrep (if present), nvidia-smi.log, kernel-info.txt
- Retention: CI artifacts kept for 30 days; nightly regression artifacts kept for 180 days.

Minimal flamegraph quality gate for CI smoke
- total_samples >= 5000 (or fail-fast with warning)
- top-5 stacks account for < 75% of samples (if >75% it's often a narrow hotspot that needs investigation)
- svg size < 15MB before upload (trim symbol tables if necessary)

Lightweight ebpf helper (ebpf-lite-attach.py) notes
- Small BPF program that counts context switches and samples thread state for a short window.
- Uses BCC (python bcc) when available; falls back to userland uprobe if kernel headers absent.
- Output: ascii summary and a small samples.json that can be folded into flamegraph input.

How to triage once you have artifacts
1) Load flamegraph.svg. Identify the tallest stacks and which module they belong to.
2) Cross-check with nsys timeline to see if CPU stacks line up with GPU queue stalls.
3) Check meta.json for image tag to reproduce exact binary.
4) Re-run with toggles (ENABLE_CACHE=0, BATCH=1) to isolate caching/batching impact.
5) If kernel symbols show up, collect perf record -e sched:sched_switch -a -o sched.data to correlate context switches.

Open questions we still want to solve (notes)
- Automatic mapping of flamegraph frames to source-level lines (DWARF is flaky in stripped images) — should we add a debug-symbols registry per CI image?
- Lightweight continuous profiling agent vs short CI snapshots: tradeoff analysis pending (cost vs signal).
- Explore providing a micro-heatmap view showing token-level latency vs cpu usage per prefix length.

Related docs and references
- runtime-trace-scripts-and-debug-runbook (for step-by-step investigation)
- profiling-smoke-regression-pipeline-and-collectors (pipeline design notes)
- external: Brendan Gregg FlameGraph repo; NVIDIA Nsight documentation; BCC/eBPF examples

Immediate next actions (for this doc)
- Luca: add the sample collect-local.sh from your tmp branch into scripts/ and link the PR here (github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/412).
- Priya: add CI snippet to .github/workflows/perf-smoke.yml with opt-in flag; wire upload to s3 staging bucket.
- Omar: prototype a tiny web viewer for flamegraphs under internal staging (optional).

Notes to self / rough TODOs (scratchpad)
- ensure all wrappers bail nicely when docker/privileges missing
- add command to cleanup governor state after profiling on CI runners
- add quick linting for generated SVGs to avoid shipping empty/invalid files

If you use anything from here, please add a short README header to the script and file a small PR linking to this doc (PROF-128).
